reading: A small multi-colour pattern sits at the left edge. A copy of it is placed flush with the right edge, and the gap between the two copies is filled, row by row, with that row's first-column colour.
verb: copy pattern to opposite edge and bridge

slots.pattern: the left block of non-background columns
slots.copy_place: flush with the right border, same rows
slots.bridge_colour: per row, the colour of the pattern's first column in that row
slots.bridge_cells: the background cells between the two copies on each row

why: on every row, output = pattern + (row's first colour repeated) + pattern, total width unchanged

reading: Each solid colour-8 rectangle is recoloured by position: its four quadrants become 6 (top-left), 1 (top-right), 2 (bottom-left), 3 (bottom-right), and the inner rectangle inset by 2 cells on every side becomes 4.

slots.subject: each solid rectangle (8-connected object)
slots.quadrant_colours: TL=6, TR=1, BL=2, BR=3 (split at half height and half width)
slots.core: cells at least 2 in from the rectangle's edge become 4

why: every rectangle cell's new colour depends only on its position inside its own rectangle; background unchanged

reading: Two opposite borders are full lines of two colours. Next to every isolated 1-cell, on the side facing the nearer of the two border lines, a cell of that border's colour is added.

slots.subject: markers (isolated cells of colour 1)
slots.borders: the two opposite full border lines (rows or columns) of distinct colours
slots.placement: the 4-neighbour of the marker in the direction of the nearer border line
slots.colour: the colour of that nearer border line

why: each marker gains exactly one neighbour, coloured as and placed toward the closer border line; nothing else changes

reading: Every object is shifted to the right by a distance equal to its own bounding-box width.
verb: shift each object right by its width
why: each object keeps its shape and rows; its column offset increases by its width

reading: Several overlapping octagonal rings of different colours (plus scattered noise cells) are drawn on a background. The output stacks one clean 6x6 ring per colour vertically, topmost (least occluded) ring first, on the input's background colour.

slots.subject: each ring colour (objects with more than a few cells; single noise cells ignored)
slots.unit: a fixed 6x6 octagon outline in that colour on background
slots.order: stacking order, top layer (fully visible) first
slots.layout: copies stacked vertically, output 6 wide and 6*N tall

why: output is N stacked 6x6 canonical rings, one per ring colour, in occlusion order

reading: A 2x2 block of four colours sits in the centre of a 4x4 grid. Each of its cells moves out to the grid corner nearest it and the centre is cleared.

slots.subject: the four cells of the central 2x2 block
slots.target: for each cell, the grid corner on its diagonal side

why: output corners hold the central block's colours in the same relative arrangement; everything else is background
invariants: relative arrangement of the four colours

reading: Colour-3 cells that are 4-connected to at least one other 3 become 8; isolated 3s (no orthogonal 3 neighbour) stay 3.

new_rows.name: paired
new_rows.datalog:
paired(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), DY = 0, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y, X2, C).
paired(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), DX = 0, Y2 = Y + DY, cell(Y2, X, C).

why: every 3 cell with an orthogonal 3 neighbour becomes 8; nothing else changes (diagonal-only contact does not count)

reading: A vertical and a horizontal line cross. The eight cells around the crossing become 4, leaving the crossing cell itself unchanged.

new_rows.name: ring
new_rows.datalog:
cross(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), Y1 = Y - 1, cell(Y1, X, A), Y2 = Y + 1, cell(Y2, X, B), X1 = X - 1, cell(Y, X1, D), X2 = X + 1, cell(Y, X2, E).
ring(Y2, X2) :- cross(Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX.

why: the 8 neighbours of the line crossing are colour 4; every other cell is unchanged
invariants: line cells away from the crossing

reading: Two 3x3 colour-2 frames with a 5 centre each have one gap in their outline. A 4-coloured corridor is drawn from each gap outward and the two corridors are joined by a filled 4 rectangle spanning the space between the frames; frame cells are not overwritten.

slots.subject: the two 3x3 frames and their gap cells
slots.path: from each gap, the cells straight out from it, joined by a solid rectangle spanning between the frames (from one frame's outside-gap line to the other's)

why: 4 cells form one connected filled region touching both gaps; frames and background elsewhere unchanged

reading: From the single 2 cell on the bottom row a two-cell-thick diagonal staircase of 2 is drawn up and to the right until the border; where the path would hit a 1 cell it is pushed to go around (beside) the obstacle and continues diagonally.

slots.source: the 2 cell on the bottom row
slots.direction: up-right diagonal, each row painting the cell and its right neighbour
slots.obstacle: 1 cells: kept, path shifts to avoid them

why: the 2 path is a connected up-right staircase from the source to the border that never covers a 1 cell
